info.title: cleanup
info.description: The routes of the cleanup module. Every path is relative to the mount the host assigns.

put.description: Checks and keeps the whole list of rules. A storage rule names a folder below the root of a storage in allowed_storages. A printer rule names a printer in allowed_devices, a folder on its storage and a pattern for print files, and only runs by hand. Every new or changed rule is checked against the signed-in person's own rights (write_storage on storages, operate on the printer) and remembers that person; an unchanged rule keeps its author. Refused with 403 when the person may not delete there and with 422 when the rule is outside the operator's lists. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

get.summary: What the rules would delete now
get.description: Scans the folders the rules cover, with the signed-in person's rights, and answers per rule how many units, files and bytes it holds and would delete. With rule, the answer for that rule also lists the paths to delete, at most 3000. A printer rule is read only when asked for alone (lazy in the overview), never while the printer prints, and never offers the file of the current or the last print. The host takes view_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

parameters.name: rule
parameters.description: The id of one rule. Absent answers the counts of every rule.

get.summary: How a storage's space is spread
get.description: The size and file count of every top-level entry of one storage in allowed_storages, largest first, listed with the signed-in person's rights. Kept for ten minutes per person unless refresh is set. The host takes view_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

post.summary: Record a cleanup the page did
post.description: The page deletes with the signed-in person's rights and reports the result here, so the history lists it. Refused with 422 for a rule that does not exist, negative counts or a rule name longer than 80. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

Runs the storage rules with the module's API token, as the schedule does: each enabled rule only while the person who saved it may still delete there. Refused with 409 when no token is set. The host takes operate_resource on the module's instance before this is called.

get.summary: The rules, the schedule and the last runs
get.description: Every rule, whether the module deletes on its own schedule and when next, why the last automatic run skipped a rule, the operator's allowed storages and printers, and the last thirty runs. The host takes view_resource on the module's instance before this is called.
